common.importReadyTitle: Review the records before the first trip
common.importReadyBody: Check imported identities, certification status and any accepted-waiver evidence. Historical visits do not create future bookings; prepare the departure and check each diver’s requirements separately.

proof.boatTitle: Call each person aboard after every dive

competitor.runTheDay: Try your crew’s next trip in DiveDay
competitor.readyToMove: See how the next departure works in DiveDay
competitor.walkDemoFirst: Walk the sample shop with your crew. When you are ready, we will review your files and the handover with you.

spreadsheet.title: Give every diver on your sheet a place on the trip
spreadsheet.heroLede: Let divers book and complete their forms, see what is missing before departure and run roll call on the boat. Start with the list you already keep; we help review the file before it becomes your roster.
spreadsheet.wedgeIntro1: If the sheet is only a customer list, you may want to keep it. Try DiveDay when checking cards, chasing waivers and copying names onto the boat list are work you still do by hand.
spreadsheet.wedgeIntro2: Compare these tasks with the way you prepare a departure now.

cardsChecked.title: Every certification checked before the boat leaves
cardsChecked.body: Each diver’s certification is read against what the trip and the site require. Anyone who can’t board yet is listed, with the reason.

blockersOnePlace.title: Who can’t board yet, in one list
blockersOnePlace.body: Needs you, on Today, lists who still can’t board and why: a missing waiver, or a certification nobody has verified yet.

diversBookThemselves.title: Divers book and sign themselves
diversBookThemselves.body: A diver picks a seat and signs the waiver from a link, with no account and no app. An unsigned one is on Today the night before, with the name.

manifestHeadCount.title: A manifest that calls the roll by name
manifestHeadCount.body: The crew marks each diver and crew member aboard by name, dive by dive, on a phone, from a copy saved to it before the boat leaves, so the roll call keeps working with no signal at the ramp.

spreadsheet.columnsIntro: One row per diver, saved as CSV. Your headings don’t have to match these; the common names are recognized, and the preview names any it isn’t sure of.

name.detail: First and last in two columns, or one full-name column. The only thing a row needs.

email.detail: How DiveDay reaches a diver and recognizes a returning one, so a second import updates instead of duplicating. A row without one still comes in.

phone.detail: Mobile or landline, however you’ve written it.

dateOfBirth.detail: A real date of birth carries over when your file has one.

emergencyContact.detail: A name and a phone number, when you have them, land on the diver’s record.

diveInsurance.detail: A DAN number or a provider name comes across as written. Never a gate; it is what the crew wants on hand in an incident.

certification.detail: Agency, level, and certification number. The certification number is what lets a record come across at all.

specialty.detail: Deep, wreck, night, or drysuit. One cell can name several (“Deep, Wreck”) and each becomes its own certification under the diver’s agency number.

nitrox.detail: A yes/no column, plus the nitrox certification number if you keep one. The number is what brings it across.

rentalSizes.detail: BCD, wetsuit, boot, and fin. Whatever sizes you track become a fit profile.

pastVisits.detail: A date, trip name, and price per row becomes that diver’s history here, so a regular arrives as a regular. Repeat their email on each row to match the right person.

waivers.detail: A signed waiver claim and safe document links can come across; individual medical answers do not.

paymentHistory.detail: Payment, refund, and receipt rows can be kept as unverified history, never as live card data.

notes.detail: Staff and diver notes become private notes on the diver’s profile.

gearHistory.detail: A separate gear CSV brings in your tagged units and dated service, hydro, inspection, O2-clean, and condition records.

spreadsheet.parallelRunNote: Keep the sheet going as long as you like. A re-import matches divers by email and updates them instead of duplicating, so the day you stop keeping it is yours to pick.
spreadsheet.closingTitle: The demo is the shop your sheet would land in
spreadsheet.closingDescription: Open it as the owner, the captain or a diver. No sign-up, and nothing in it is yours to break.

concierge.eyebrow: A person does the import with you
concierge.title: We’ll review the move with you
concierge.description: Send us what you have, whether a clean export or a decade of messy tabs, and we’ll map the columns and bring your divers in with you, free. If DiveDay is ever the wrong fit, we’ll help you carry it all back out the same way.

alongside.title: Keep what works. Add what your dive day is missing
alongside.heroLede: You don’t have to leave anything to start. Run a single departure through DiveDay while the booking site, the register, and the sheet you already use keep doing their jobs, then decide what to move.
alongside.intro1: DiveDay has no live link to other software. It has no retail register and doesn’t talk to your booking site on its own. What it has is files in, files out, a booking link you control, and a browser extension that looks up cards on your agency’s own page, so the two sides meet where a person can see them.
alongside.intro2: So the useful question isn’t what DiveDay plugs into. It’s which part of the day each tool should own while you try it.

booking.title: Your booking site or channel
booking.body: Keep taking bookings there. When one lands, seat the diver in DiveDay so the waiver, the card check, and the manifest start from a real person. Check changes and cancellations on each side.

register.title: Your register or retail system
register.body: Keep it. DiveDay doesn’t ring up retail or count stock. An order can carry a retail line, and card payments run through your own Stripe account.

sheet.title: Your spreadsheet or contact list
sheet.body: Keep it as long as it helps. Import it whenever you want divers, cards, sizes, and past visits in DiveDay. Importing a file again updates the same people, matched on email.

waivers.title: Your waiver or forms tool
waivers.body: Divers sign the release DiveDay sends. Waivers you already hold come across in the import when your export includes them.

agency.title: Your certification agency
agency.body: DiveDay has no agency account of its own. Staff check a diver’s card in one click with the DiveDay browser extension, which looks it up on the agency’s own page from their browser, and confirm it in DiveDay. Submitting new certifications stays with the agency.

website.title: Your own website
website.body: Paste DiveDay’s schedule and booking pieces into your own site, or point your booking link at DiveDay and leave the site as it is.

one.title: Pick one departure
one.body: Seat its divers in DiveDay and run it from there: waivers, card checks, and the manifest.

two.title: Leave the rest where it is
two.body: Your booking site, register and sheet carry on as before. Compare that morning at the dock with the one before it.

three.title: Move more when it’s easier
three.body: Not before. Your records leave with one export button at any time, so trying DiveDay never traps them.

alongside.closingTitle: Try one departure alongside what you have
alongside.closingDescription: Look around the demo, or send us a sample of your records and we’ll review the move with you.
